as_told.title: NASA study of Alcubierre's warp model

plain: NASA is said to have studied warp drive, a theoretical way for a spacecraft to travel by bending space itself. Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the National Security Agency, mentions it to Michels while discussing his book The Shadow of Time, saying "we go through NASA's innovative propulsion program, which I think is fantastic." Michels tells his own version on another episode. He says the physicist Miguel Alcubierre "figured out this sort of theoretical model," that "NASA's been studying this for years," and that a NASA scientist named Harold "Sonny" White has done "interesting work in this area." Neither gives details of how the programme worked or what it found. They raise it because, if true, a government space agency takes faster-than-light travel seriously.
